policy_types.name: AI Acceptable Use Policy
policy_types.description: Defines permitted and prohibited uses of AI tools within the institution

sections.title: Purpose and Scope
sections.copilot_instruction: Write a purpose statement explaining why this policy exists, what it covers, and who it applies to. Reference the institution's strategic context and the framework's overview.

sections.title: Definitions
sections.copilot_instruction: Define key terms: artificial intelligence, generative AI, high-risk AI system, AI literacy. Use definitions from the regulatory context for the user's region.

sections.title: Permitted Uses
sections.copilot_instruction: List permitted uses of AI tools based on the framework competency blocks at the institution's current and target maturity levels. Be specific about which tools and contexts are approved.

sections.title: Prohibited Uses
sections.copilot_instruction: List prohibited uses based on EU Art.5 prohibitions (if EU region) and framework ethics dimension indicators. Include emotion recognition bans in education contexts.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities
sections.copilot_instruction: Define roles and responsibilities for AI governance based on framework governance indicators. Include senior leadership, IT, academic staff, and students.

sections.title: Data Protection and Privacy
sections.copilot_instruction: Address data protection requirements using GDPR/FERPA/UK GDPR provisions from the regulatory context. Cover consent, data minimisation, and student data.

sections.title: Academic Integrity
sections.copilot_instruction: Address AI use in assessments. Define expectations for disclosure, attribution, and what constitutes academic misconduct involving AI.

sections.title: Monitoring and Review
sections.copilot_instruction: Define monitoring mechanisms and review schedules. Reference EU Art.26 deployer obligations if applicable.

sections.title: Training Requirements
sections.copilot_instruction: Define AI literacy training requirements based on EU Art.4 obligations and the institution's individual framework learning objectives.

sections.title: Review Schedule
sections.copilot_instruction: Recommend an annual review schedule with triggers for interim review (e.g., significant regulatory change, major AI incident).

policy_types.name: AI Governance Policy
policy_types.description: Establishes strategic AI governance structures, risk management, and accountability frameworks
policy_types.target_audience: Senior leadership, governance boards, IT directors

sections.title: Governance Structure and Accountability
sections.copilot_instruction: Define the AI governance structure including committees, roles, and reporting lines. Reference UNESCO Policy dimensions 1 and 3, and institutional framework governance blocks.

sections.title: AI Risk Classification Process
sections.copilot_instruction: Define how the institution classifies AI systems by risk level. Reference EU Annex III mapping and institutional framework risk indicators.

sections.title: Procurement and Validation of AI Tools
sections.copilot_instruction: Define procurement criteria for AI tools including safety standards, accessibility, and pedagogical value. Reference DfE product safety standards (UK) if applicable.

sections.title: Human Oversight Requirements
sections.copilot_instruction: Define human oversight requirements for AI systems. Reference EU Art.14 and framework oversight indicators.

sections.title: Incident Reporting and Response
sections.copilot_instruction: Define incident reporting procedures for AI-related issues. Reference EU Art.26 deployer obligations.

sections.title: Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment
sections.copilot_instruction: Define when and how to conduct fundamental rights impact assessments for AI deployments. Reference EU Art.27 requirements for public institutions.

sections.title: Staff AI Literacy Programme
sections.copilot_instruction: Define the AI literacy programme based on EU Art.4 requirements and the institution's individual framework competency targets.

sections.title: Monitoring, Evaluation and Continuous Improvement
sections.copilot_instruction: Define monitoring and evaluation frameworks. Reference UNESCO Policy dimension 6 and framework monitoring indicators.

policy_types.name: AI Assessment Integrity Policy
policy_types.description: Governs the use of AI in educational assessment, including academic integrity and AI-assisted marking
policy_types.target_audience: Academic staff, quality assurance teams, students

sections.title: Principles for AI in Assessment
sections.copilot_instruction: Establish core principles for AI use in assessment including fairness, transparency, and maintaining academic standards.

sections.title: Classification of AI Use in Assessment
sections.copilot_instruction: Define categories of AI use in assessment (formative vs summative, permitted vs restricted). Reference EU Annex III 3(b) classification.

sections.title: Student Expectations and Disclosure
sections.copilot_instruction: Define student obligations for AI disclosure and attribution. Reference EU Art.50 transparency requirements.

sections.title: Detection and Response to AI Misuse
sections.copilot_instruction: Define how AI misuse in assessment will be detected and handled. Include graduated response procedures.

sections.title: AI-Assisted Marking and Feedback Guidelines
sections.copilot_instruction: Define guidelines for using AI in marking and feedback. Reference DfE guidance (UK) and framework assessment blocks.

sections.title: Exam Proctoring Policy
sections.copilot_instruction: Address AI-based proctoring with reference to EU Art.5 emotion recognition ban and Annex III 3(d).

sections.title: Appeals Process
sections.copilot_instruction: Define appeals procedures for AI-related assessment decisions.

policy_types.name: Staff AI Development Policy
policy_types.description: Defines AI literacy requirements, training programmes, and professional development pathways for staff
policy_types.target_audience: HR, professional development teams, all staff

sections.title: AI Literacy Requirements and Timeline
sections.copilot_instruction: Define mandatory AI literacy requirements with implementation timeline. Reference EU Art.4 obligations and the individual framework's progression levels.

sections.title: Competency Framework Alignment
sections.copilot_instruction: Map training requirements to the user's selected individual competency framework (e.g., UNESCO Teacher, BDC, DigComp).

sections.title: Training Programme Structure
sections.copilot_instruction: Design a training programme structure mapped to framework learning objectives and progression levels.

sections.title: Role-Specific Pathways
sections.copilot_instruction: Define role-specific development pathways using framework role-specific content (e.g., BDC profiles, ISTE audience variants).

sections.title: Recognition and Certification
sections.copilot_instruction: Define how progression through the framework levels translates to recognition and certification milestones.

sections.title: Ongoing CPD and Review
sections.copilot_instruction: Define ongoing CPD expectations with the framework's highest-level descriptors as long-term targets.

policy_types.name: AI Data Governance Policy
policy_types.description: Governs data processing, protection, and privacy in AI systems used by the institution
policy_types.target_audience: Data protection officers, IT teams, senior leadership

sections.title: Data Classification and Sensitivity
sections.copilot_instruction: Define data classification categories and sensitivity levels relevant to AI processing. Reference GDPR/FERPA categories.

sections.title: Consent and Transparency
sections.copilot_instruction: Define consent requirements and transparency obligations for AI data processing. Reference EU Art.13.

sections.title: AI System Data Inventory
sections.copilot_instruction: Define requirements for maintaining an inventory of AI systems and their data flows. Reference framework infrastructure/operations indicators.

sections.title: Data Protection Impact Assessments
sections.copilot_instruction: Define when and how DPIAs should be conducted for AI systems. Reference regulatory DPIA requirements.

sections.title: Third-Party Data Sharing
sections.copilot_instruction: Define policies for sharing data with third-party AI providers. Include due diligence and contractual requirements.

sections.title: Retention and Deletion
sections.copilot_instruction: Define data retention periods and deletion procedures for AI-processed data.

sections.title: Student Data Specific Provisions
sections.copilot_instruction: Define specific protections for student data in AI systems. Reference FERPA (US), UK GDPR children's provisions, and age-appropriate access controls.

policy_types.name: Student AI Guidance
policy_types.description: Student-facing guidance on responsible and effective use of AI tools in learning

sections.title: What AI Tools Are and How They Work
sections.copilot_instruction: Explain what AI tools are and how they work in plain, student-friendly language. Draw from AI literacy framework content.

sections.title: When You Can and Cannot Use AI
sections.copilot_instruction: Clearly define when AI use is permitted and when it is not. Cross-reference the institution's acceptable use policy.

sections.title: Academic Integrity and AI
sections.copilot_instruction: Explain academic integrity expectations regarding AI use. Define disclosure, attribution, and what constitutes misconduct.

sections.title: Protecting Your Data and Privacy
sections.copilot_instruction: Advise students on protecting their personal data when using AI tools. Draw from digital citizenship framework blocks.

sections.title: Critical Evaluation of AI Outputs
sections.copilot_instruction: Teach students to critically evaluate AI-generated content. Reference critical thinking framework blocks.

sections.title: Reporting Concerns
sections.copilot_instruction: Explain how students can report concerns about AI tools or their misuse.

sections.title: Where to Learn More
sections.copilot_instruction: Provide links and resources for further AI literacy learning. Flag as [NEEDS INSTITUTIONAL INPUT] for institution-specific resources.
